articles.title: Apple's new CEO John Ternus to face first earnings test as memory costs surge
articles.desc: Ternus, who took the reins from Tim Cook in September, has overseen the introduction of Apple's first foldable phone, smart home hub and Apple's first touch-screen laptops. All of those products began shipping during the company's current fiscal first quarter, amid what Cook had called a "100-year flood" of rising memory costs.

articles.title: Zen Technologies shares rally 9% after Q2 profit rises 51% YoY, revenue nearly doubles
articles.desc: Zen Technologies shares jumped 8.67% after the defence technology company reported a 51% YoY rise in Q2 net profit to Rs 90 crore, while revenue surged 98% to Rs 345 crore. The company recorded an order inflow of Rs 481.81 crore during the quarter, taking its consolidated order book to Rs 1,375.70 crore as of September 30, 2026.

articles.title: FII retreat deepens: Almost every second Nifty stock sees stake cuts in all 3 quarters of 2026
articles.desc: This year has seen Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs) divest nearly ₹3 lakh crore in Indian equities, causing a significant reduction in their stakes. As a result, FII ownership has declined in about half of the Nifty stocks over the past three quarters. Meanwhile, Domestic Institutional Investors (DIIs) have increased their equity holdings, reflecting a change in market dynamics amidst frequent foreign sell-offs.

articles.title: Why is market rallying today? Sensex soars 1,000 pts, Nifty above 23,300. 7 factors driving Rs 6 lakh crore D-Street gains
articles.desc: The Indian stock market saw a robust performance on Monday, with Sensex and Nifty climbing over 1%. This was largely driven by Reliance Industries' strong earnings report, which propelled its shares upwards. Overall, sectors like Nifty Oil & Gas thrived, although Nifty Pharma lagged behind. Market breadth revealed more winners than losers, reflecting investor confidence, even amid some sectors' struggles in the dynamic exchange environment.

articles.title: Japan's Nikkei slips as Kioxia tumbles 13%; Tokyo Electron, Panasonic limit losses
articles.desc: Japan’s Nikkei slipped as Kioxia plunged 13.29% following a disappointing earnings outlook, while banking stocks also weakened. Gains in Tokyo Electron and Panasonic, supported by upbeat profit forecasts and AI-related demand, limited losses. Broader investor sentiment remained cautious following Wall Street’s technology selloff and concerns over AI investment sustainability.

articles.title: US Midterm elections, Apple earnings, jobs data to test Wall Street after AI rout
articles.desc: Wall Street faces a pivotal week as US midterm elections, major corporate earnings and October jobs data test investor sentiment. Apple, AMD and Palantir results, alongside regulatory uncertainty and economic signals, could determine market direction and volatility.

articles.title: NTPC shares rise 3% after Q2 results. Why Jefferies and Nuvama remain bullish
articles.desc: NTPC shares rose after the state-owned power major reported a 14% YoY rise in standalone net profit to Rs 5,320 crore for Q2 FY27. Revenue grew 17% to Rs 45,752 crore, while EBITDA increased 9% to Rs 10,891 crore. The company also announced an interim dividend of Rs 3 per share, with November 6 set as the record date. Brokerages maintained their Buy ratings on the stock.

articles.title: Jio Platforms shares climb over 3% after Q2 PAT rises 14% YoY to Rs 8,389 crore. Buy, sell or hold?

articles.desc: India's GST collections in October reached ₹2.31 lakh crore, reflecting a 22.9% year-on-year increase. Strong consumption trends are indicated by rising passenger car sales and record digital payments. Power consumption also surged nearly 22% compared to last year, further emphasizing economic strength. Despite a high inflation rate of 5.5%, demand has remained robust, supporting growth forecasts. Analysts suggest this growth aligns with leading indicators of a consumption-driven economy.

articles.title: One nation, many opportunities: Why India's many elections may be keeping protests peaceful
articles.desc: People across India are protesting peacefully, contrasting with violent agitations seen in other countries. The 'one nation, multiple elections' framework allows diverse political benefits to be shared among parties. This electoral model keeps governments accountable and responsive to public needs. Elections help to channel frustrations and enable citizens to express their concerns. As a result, the political landscape remains dynamic and participatory, fostering a sense of empowerment.

articles.title: PM Modi to meet Niti Aayog leadership on Nov 5; likely to  review  work as govt begins shaping  FY28 Budget
articles.desc: Prime Minister Narendra Modi is scheduled to meet the new leadership of Niti Aayog on November 5. This meeting aims to establish budget priorities amidst global uncertainty and economic growth challenges. The focus will be on enhancing domestic manufacturing and creating employment opportunities. Experts from various sectors will provide insights related to India's development objectives.

articles.desc: CII has called for extending the GST Council's approach to decriminalise offences in various sectors. This move aims to enhance ease of doing business and attract investments in land, labour, and construction. The organisation emphasizes the importance of simplifying regulatory processes across different government tiers.

articles.title: Sebi to delist penny stocks: Market regulator plans AI-based surveillance of such firms
articles.desc: The Securities and Exchange Board of India plans to delist companies that have no economic activity. This move aims to protect investors, especially those investing in penny stocks. The regulator highlights the potential dangers posed by such inactive companies in the market. Additionally, Sebi intends to announce compliance requirements for foreign institutional investors soon.

articles.title: Mansukh Mandaviya rolls out EPFO services on WhatsApp, starts auto-settlement of small inoperative accounts
articles.desc: Union Labour & Employment Minister Mansukh Mandaviya launched EPFO services through WhatsApp for easier access. Subscribers can check their PF balance and transaction history conveniently using this platform. The automatic settlement for inoperative EPF accounts was also introduced, streamlining the process for beneficiaries. In total, around one lakh accounts will benefit from this initiative. The EPFO's commitment to evolve and focus on worker-centric innovations was emphasized during the celebration.

articles.title: EAM Jaishankar discusses Ukraine-Russia conflict solutions amid G20 summit
articles.desc: India has engaged in discussions with Russia, Europe, and Ukraine regarding the ongoing conflict and its impact. These talks focused on preventing attacks on civilian shipping and restoring grain exports affected by Black Sea disruptions. External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar emphasised the complexity of discussions around ceasing attacks on energy installations. Various interpretations of what constitutes energy installations have complicated these discussions.

articles.title: Kashmiri apple supplies fall short of Diwali demand amid fungal outbreak
articles.desc: Supply of Kashmiri apples is currently inadequate due to a significant scab outbreak that has affected this year's crop. The primary concern is that a large percentage of apples arriving in markets are of lower grades. Growers are facing high production costs while receiving low returns on affected apples. Demand remains good ahead of Diwali, with higher-quality apples commanding good prices.

articles.title: Festive spending drives record UPI transactions in October
articles.desc: UPI processed transactions worth Rs 31.53 lakh crore during the month, a 16% rise from a year earlier and the highest on record, signalling that the platform continues to expand even as consumers navigate higher prices of electronics and other festive purchases this year.

articles.title: India's October Gross GST collections jump 22.9% to Rs 2.31 lakh crore
articles.desc: India's gross GST collection reached Rs 2.31 lakh crore in October, representing a 22.9% increase from last year. The gross GST collected for the April-October period totaled Rs 14.78 lakh crore, showing a 13.2% growth year-on-year. Maharashtra recorded the highest revenue for October at Rs 35,150 crore, followed by Karnataka and Gujarat. Some states, including Sikkim and Ladakh, experienced significant declines in GST collections during the month.

articles.title: Fuel, forex and farmers: Why India is betting big on maize
